patch.value: The Windows nightly leg cannot separate product defects from harness noise: 744 hardcoded POSIX path literals and 203 raw errno strings in the suite fail on Windows for reasons unrelated to pm behaviour

GH-791 (windows-latest / Node 24, commit d885d5a0) fails four tests. Exactly one of them is a product defect - the merge-safety workspace_root canonicalization tracked as pm-ihmfs6, which also fails on macOS. The other three are properties of the suite, not of pm:

1. tests/unit/sdk/merge-safety.spec.ts 'installs idempotent git attributes/config and exercises the CLI adapter' - same path-spelling family as pm-ihmfs6.
2. tests/unit/packages/guide-shell-runtime.spec.ts 'builds completion registries and list helpers across schema shapes' - asserts listAllItemMetadata was called with the literal '/tmp/pm' (lines 24, 28, 120, 136, 142). On Windows path.resolve('/tmp/pm') is C:\tmp\pm, so the assertion cannot hold and never could.
3. tests/unit/sdk/context-integrity-primitives.spec.ts 'invalidates derived drift state after conventional history writes' - asserts the warning string history_drift_cache_invalidation_failed:ENOTDIR. Windows raises a different errno for the same condition. This one has a product tail worth deciding separately: the diagnostic code embeds a raw platform errno, so the warning an agent parses is platform-dependent.

Census of the class across tests/: 744 hardcoded POSIX absolute path literals matching "/(tmp|home|var|usr)/ in 81 files (worst: extension-loader.spec.ts 159, search-command.spec.ts 137, extensions-runtime.spec.ts 48, builtin-extension-entrypoints.spec.ts 39, telemetry-runtime.spec.ts 34, settings-store.spec.ts 30), plus 203 raw errno literals.

Why this matters more than tidiness: the Windows leg has been red often enough (pm-e70zh5 records a 32/84 scheduled-run failure rate) that a red leg carries no information. Today it is red for one real cross-platform defect and three artifacts, and nothing in the failure output distinguishes them - somebody has to read four stack traces to learn that. The suite is asserting on the harness's temp-directory conventions rather than on pm, so a genuine Windows regression would arrive already camouflaged.

Remedy: route path literals through the existing helpers (withTempPmPath, mockPosixPath) or path.join from os.tmpdir(), and assert on normalized error classes rather than raw errno strings. Prefer a lint rule or a gate over a one-time sweep, since the count grows with every new spec.
No test asserts on a hardcoded POSIX absolute path or a raw platform errno string; a red Windows nightly leg names only product defects

Cross-platform nightly is GREEN on main again, verified by dispatch 2026-07-28. Run 30372071932 on main succeeded in 7m31s with every leg passing, immediately after PR#795 merged at 14:20:36Z.

The preceding red streak was pre-fix, not an unowned regression: the last three scheduled runs on main failed (30334992958 at 06:29Z today, 30246735868 on 07-27, 30191427127 on 07-26), all on the same two legs, macos-latest Node 24 and windows-latest Node 24, and the actual failures were four specs — guide-shell-runtime building completion registries across schema shapes, context-integrity-primitives invalidating derived drift state after conventional history writes, and merge-safety twice for installing idempotent git attributes and for preferring explicit tracker paths over protected source coordinates. Every scheduled run predated the merge, and PR#795's own branch was named for this work and had already been verified by dispatch, run 30361026722 passing at 12:54Z.

The durable lesson for this item rather than the incident: a scheduled-only signal necessarily reports a stale verdict for as long as the interval, so a red nightly on main is not evidence of a live defect until the last completed run postdates the last merge. Confirm by dispatch before filing anything, and compare the run start against the merge timestamp rather than against the calendar day.

Nightly leg status enumerated 2026-07-29. The scheduled run at 06:34 UTC, run id 30428599608, failed. Exactly one leg is red: Nightly on windows-latest with Node 24. Every other leg in the matrix succeeded.

Two specs fail on that leg and no others:

tests/unit/commands/test-command.spec.ts, runTest, "terminates stubborn timed-out linked commands without hanging" - failed after 3,693 ms, which is the timeout itself rather than an assertion. This one is a product-behaviour candidate, not spec noise: if a stubborn child cannot be killed on Windows, linked-test timeout enforcement does not work there, and the precedent in this class is explicit that the fix must not be spec-side only.

tests/unit/sdk/workspace-snapshot.spec.ts, workspace snapshots, "rejects non-file filesystem entries in authoritative state" - failed in 93 ms, an assertion failure on filesystem-entry classification. This is on the snapshot surface that shipped on 2026-07-28, so the class is still acquiring new members as new surfaces land, which is the argument for the portability sweep this item owns rather than another point patch.

Nightly verdict recorded 2026-07-30. The 06:30Z scheduled run 30519801227 was RED on exactly one leg (windows-latest, Node 24) and exactly one spec: tests/unit/core/store/item-store-root-contract.spec.ts > item metadata tracker-root contract > rejects a regular file root with a stable typed diagnostic. Test Files 1 failed / 396 passed. That run started at 06:30Z; PR 823, which fixes precisely that contract by inspecting existing ancestors after ENOENT, merged at 08:52Z. So the red window was pre-fix, not a HEAD regression.

Verified by dispatch rather than by inference: workflow_dispatch run 30529480380 on main is GREEN on all five legs (ubuntu Node 22, ubuntu Node 24, ubuntu Node 25, macos Node 24, windows Node 24). HEAD is clean on the Windows leg.

Residual worth noting for this item's scope: the same nightly log shows two MCP contract-violation warnings emitted by our own integration suite and failing nothing - Unknown option "full" for pm_update action "update" and Unknown option "dryRun" for pm_run action "test-all". Neither option is declared by the CLI either (pm update has no --full, pm test-all has no --dry-run), so these are suite-side arguments that no contract knows. The warning fires on every nightly and no gate escalates it.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Nightly signal at HEAD, 2026-07-30 (evening). Dispatched a nightly run at 87d88c5e, which is the merge commit for the context-budget bundle and therefore the first commit that carries it through the full matrix. Result: success, all legs. The scheduled run at 06:30Z that failed was on a72725b0, which predates the Windows tracker root-contract fix, so that red is explained by commit rather than by flake and is not a live failure surface.

The pattern worth keeping on this item: a scheduled nightly failure and a dispatched nightly success on the same day are not a contradiction when the schedule fired on an older commit. Reading the head SHA of the failing run before triaging the failure is the cheapest way to avoid re-investigating a fix that already landed. Two consecutive passes have now resolved a nightly red this way.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Family measurement 2026-08-03, recorded here because this item owns the Windows leg and the number is about the family rather than any one spec.

Scheduled Nightly Validation raised 28 failure alerts between 2026-06-20 and 2026-08-03: 19 on windows-latest Node 24, 6 on macos-latest Node 24, 3 on ubuntu. Those fall on 23 distinct calendar days inside a 44-day window. All 28 are closed, median repair 5.7 hours, maximum 175 hours. A title census of the tracker returns roughly thirty closed items in the same class over a longer span, each with a different root cause.

The most recent occurrence, run on 2026-08-03 at 07:30Z, failed one spec in the agent runtime provenance suite: the Windows branch of a test that derives its own expected workspace slug by restating the production transform. The product fix for that slug landed at 08:39Z the same morning and the alert issue was closed at 09:30Z, so the leg is not known to be red at current HEAD and the next scheduled run is the first evidence that will say so. Nothing here claims a live red.

What the number changes is the framing. Each repair is proportionate when judged against one failing spec and disproportionate when judged against a family that returns on half of all days. The rate itself, its recurrence identity, and the threshold that should change behaviour are now owned separately and cited from here, so this item can stay on the POSIX-literal census it was scoped to.
